summary: Windsor County, VT summit lookout: 1921 cabin and tower, a 54-ft steel tower in 1940, a 25-ft observation tower near the summit today; FFLA and the state park disagree on which structure stands.

facts.design: Steel fire tower, 54 ft to the cabin floor on a 25-ft square base (1940); the summit observation tower today is 25 ft
facts.status_note: Original summit tower listed Tower Gone; the state park describes a 25-ft observation tower near the summit; FFLA lists a relocated observation tower as standing. Sources disagree on which structure is which.

access.note: Inside Mt. Ascutney State Park; summit reached by the paved Mountain Road and four trails. The sources give no rules for climbing the observation tower.

visit.trail_note: Four major trails, about 12 miles in total, start at the base and climb to the summit

events.note: Cabin and tower built on the mountain (11th Biennial Report, as quoted by Forest Lookouts); a June 1921 item says no tower had stood there before
Steel lookout tower 54 ft to the cabin floor, erected by a side camp from the Plymouth CCC Camp; a July 1940 newspaper credits the CCC
July 1940 newspaper: a watchman would be stationed in the tower during the greatest fire danger (planned; staffing not confirmed)
Light copper roofs blew off and were replaced with galvanized iron (report for the term ending June 30, 1942)
State park gives 1952 as the end of fire tower/lookout use
Vermont Forest Service report for 1957-58: lookout facilities at the secondary stations, including Ascutney, continued on an inactive basis
Former fire tower at the summit shortened and turned into an observation platform (no date; described in a 2016 guide)
FFLA lists the original Mount Ascutney tower as Tower Gone; no date given
FFLA lists a relocated Mount Ascutney observation tower as Standing; no source read describes the move

corrections.why: Forest Lookouts gives 'Vermont - Windsor County - Ascutney State Park' and the state park page says 'Windsor County'; 'Windson' is a typo that the FFLA list repeats.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the original summit tower as gone and a relocated observation tower as standing. The state park and Happy Vermont describe a fire tower at the summit that was shortened to about 25 ft. The sources do not say whether these describe the same structure, so the story reports both accounts.
The state park gives 1952 as the end of fire tower use; a 1957-58 state report describes the lookout facilities as continued on an inactive basis. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The 1921 and 1940 history, staffing plans and 1942 roof repair come from one Forest Lookouts page that quotes newspapers and state reports. Today's structure is the open question: FFLA says the original is gone and a relocated observation tower stands; the state park and Happy Vermont describe a shortened summit tower. Height: facts.height_m is 16.5 (54 ft to the cabin floor, the 1940 tower). The parent brief's height_m of 7.6 is today's 25-ft observation tower; the editor should decide which the lookout record carries. Coordinates differ between sources (FFLA gives 43.44363, -72.45438 for the original and 43.44434, -72.45409 for the relocated; the brief also lists 43.4373, -72.4515 from Forest Lookouts); not resolved. Agency: the brief lists Ascutney State Park; the 1940 tower was erected by the Vermont Forest Service, and the park is the present custodian. Child record us-vt-mount-ascutney-moved (researched 2026-10-09) covers the relocated observation tower; this parent story covers both. No photos searched.
